Principal limitation: The clarification resolves the self-cleansing allegation more effectively than the separate question whether imposed temporal suffering constitutes satisfaction additional to Christ's work, so its conceptual distinction does not settle every historical component White introduced. Live burden: Horn still must reconcile passive cleansing with treasury merit, indulgences, and finite punishment, demonstrating that these practices neither expand the defended doctrine nor compromise the sufficiency of atonement.
